memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If a Levite moves from one of your towns anywhere in Israel where he is living, and comes in all earnestness to the place the Lord will choose, he may minister in the name of the Lord his God like all his fellow Levites who serve there in the presence of the Lord. He is to share equally in their benefits, even though he has received money from the sale of family possessions. - Deut 18:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God made sure that any Levite who came, earnestly desiring to serve at the central place of worship, would be welcomed and share equally in the provisions with the other Levites. No willing servant of God would be turned away or treated as less. His eagerness to minister was to be honoured, and his needs met alongside the rest.

There is real beauty in this. God valued a willing, earnest heart. The phrase "in all earnestness" matters, this was about Levites who genuinely longed to serve the Lord, and God made room for them and provided for them fairly.

This reflects something wonderful about God's kingdom. He welcomes all who come to Him with earnest, willing hearts, and He does not create a hierarchy where some are treated as second-class. In Christ, every believer is invited to serve and to share fully in the family of God (Gal 3:28). No one who comes to Him sincerely is turned away or made to feel unwanted. Jesus said that whoever comes to Him He will never cast out (John 6:37). Whatever your background or history, God welcomes your earnest desire to serve and love Him. Do you come to God with that kind of earnestness, trusting that He will receive you gladly?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you come to God with an earnest, willing heart?
2. Where have you felt unwelcome, and how does God's welcome heal that?
3. How can you help others feel welcomed to serve?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You welcome all who come to You earnestly. Give me a willing heart to serve, and help me welcome others. Amen.
